horwich.snapshot: Horwich, on the north-western edge of Bolton, sits in the middle of a busy full-fibre build, and the trade that does the work splits two ways. National build contractors and structured-cabling firms run fleets of engineers and order through trade accounts, while ex-BT sole traders and one-van broadband and CCTV installers order direct online with no account. We run both routes side by side so every crew and every single-hander gets kitted the same way.
horwich.s1_head: Kitting the field engineers of Greater Manchester
s1loc: Horwich is part of the wider Bolton full-fibre build, where more than thirty thousand homes and businesses across Bolton, Horwich and Westhoughton can already reach gigabit speeds. Openreach has pushed fibre out through Horwich, Blackrod, Lostock and Middlebrook, CityFibre is building across a large slice of the borough alongside its delivery partners, and Virgin Media keeps upgrading on top. Build contractors and civils crews are a regular sight working the streets, footways and cabinets from the town centre out toward Rivington and the M61 at junction six, splicing and pulling fibre into each new estate.

Alongside the residential rollout sits a solid commercial scene. Middlebrook, the huge retail, leisure and business park off De Havilland Way, plus the trade and industrial units around Chorley New Road and Lostock, give structured-cabling and CCTV firms a steady run of offices, warehouses and units to wire in Cat5e, Cat6 and fibre. Add the shops, gyms and the Bolton Wanderers stadium at Middlebrook, the schools across Horwich and a long tail of small businesses, and there is constant demand for network points, door entry and camera installs across the town.
